confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from five web searches, using search-result summaries rather than full page reads. Expatistan gave a pub beer of ARS 5,966 (~US$3.9), an expat-area cappuccino of ARS 6,300-8,600, a downtown-club cocktail of ARS 13,203, a pub dinner for two of ~US$52 and a lunch menu of ~AU$26. Preciosmundi and MyLifeElsewhere gave a domestic beer of ~US$3.8-4.0. Bootsnall gave a restaurant glass of Malbec at US$4-8. Argentine press gave cafe con leche at ARS 3,500-5,000. I could not retrieve Numbeo's own table. Sources disagree on coffee and cocktails, and peso inflation is high (~1,480-1,530 ARS/USD), so those anchors are triangulated. The two meal anchors are partly inflation-adjusted extrapolations. Cocktail (~2x beer) and wine glass (~1.35x beer) lean on the local beer relationship. The RBA rate (18 Nov 2026, 0.6720 USD per AUD) is as reported in search results for the RBA exchange-rates page. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, not from live booking pages or listings.
comparable_city_reasoning: Buenos Aires-specific aggregated price sources were prioritised for food and drink. Accommodation was set by analogy with other Southern Cone capitals (e.g. Santiago, Montevideo), adjusted for the peso's real appreciation. That puts Buenos Aires in the mid-range for Latin America in USD terms.
